sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Anti-HA and anti-HLA flow cytometry on 721.221 cells: surface expression pattern of HA-tagged HLA-C was indistinguishable from non-tagged HLA-C constructs. No peptide-presentation or T-cell activation assay reported in these clips.
sites.rationale: HLA-C is the closest ortholog of HLA-A within the classical MHC class I family, sharing the same signal-peptide/ectodomain/TM/cytoplasmic topology and nearly identical domain boundaries. The published HA insertion 'just after the signal peptide sequence' of HLA-C maps by structural equivalence to the HLA-A mature N-terminus, which begins at residue 25 (G); the tag therefore goes after residue 24 (A, the last signal-peptide residue). Python verification confirms seq[23]='A' and seq[24]='G'. The extracellular span (residues 25–307, 283 aa) is far from the TM boundary, making this terminus sterically accessible. Evidence is indirect (ortholog), so position_evidence is 'inferred' and cited_tag_residue is null. Full-length HLA-C*05 and HLA-C*07 constructs (exons 1–8) with an HA tag inserted just after the signal peptide were expressed in 721.221 cells via lentiviral transduction. HLA-C is a close ortholog of HLA-A (both MHC class I alpha chains with identical domain architecture and signal-peptide topology). The HA tag position in HLA-C corresponds structurally to insert_after_residue=24 in HLA-A (last residue of the HLA-A signal peptide, computed from the canonical sequence). Surface HA signal was detected by flow cytometry using anti-HA antibody on GFP+ cells.

sources.claim: Importantly, the expression difference between C*05 and C*07 was seen to be consistent between HA-tagged and non-tagged HLA-C constructs, suggesting that the HA tag, itself, does not change the HLA-C expression pattern or cellular characteristics, also shown by a previous study comparing HA-tagged and non-tagged HLA class I molecules 23 .

literature_notes: All four ledger lines (L1–L4) derive from a single paper (PMC5490200) and report HA-tag insertion at the N-terminus of HLA-C*05 and HLA-C*07, not HLA-A itself. HLA-C qualifies as a close ortholog (same MHC class I alpha-chain family, same topology, same signal-peptide architecture), so the evidence is indirect. No ledger line reports any insertion in HLA-A directly, nor any internal loop insertion, nor any intracellular or function-abrogating position for HLA-A. The note in L4 that 'a previous study comparing HA-tagged and non-tagged HLA class I molecules' also found no effect further supports class-I-wide tolerance of this N-terminal position, but that prior study is not itself in the ledger and cannot be cited. No other sites are supported by the ledger.
